tested_on.host: Hermes agent on an openclawlaunch Linux container: 16 vCPU, 62 GiB RAM, 39 GB free disk at slice start (headless-Linux numbers only; real-device behavior is NOT_RUN)

ocr_engine.chosen: tesseract.js 7.0.0 (Apache-2.0) + tesseract.js-core 7.0.0 (Apache-2.0), OEM LSTM_ONLY, default page segmentation

bench_only_models_not_shipped.note: PP-OCRv4 ONNX models were used only inside the dev/test-only measurement bench (rejected candidate); they are downloaded to .cache/models/ppocr (gitignored), never bundled.
bench_only_models_not_shipped.sha256s: see .cache/models/ppocr/sha256.txt recorded during the bench run

version_resolution_notes: All versions resolved at build time from the npm registry and pinned in package-lock.json.
TypeScript 7.0.2 is the registry latest, but typescript-eslint 8.73.0 declares peer support for typescript <6.1.0, so 5.9.3 is the latest mutually compatible TypeScript and was pinned.

eslint 10.15.0 is the registry latest and typescript-eslint's peer range does admit it; eslint 9.39.5 was pinned first and the suite is green on it — switching majors mid-slice would be churn without a driver, so 9.x ships S0.
onnxruntime-web 1.31.1 is a devDependency used only by the OCR selection bench; it is not part of the shipped app while Tesseract.js is the chosen engine.
npm 12 blocked the postinstall scripts of tesseract.js and protobufjs (both are cosmetic banners); both were denied via npm install-scripts deny, recorded in package.json for reproducible npm ci.
